title: Kitgen quickflow templates + probe notes (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft for a small, composable set of "quickflow" templates (KitGen) that let a new integrator get from zero to an instrumented sample app calling Redwood in under 12 minutes. Focus: minimal friction, reproducible telemetry, clear failure modes, and a tiny matrix of language/runtime examples (node/python/go).

Audience:
- Developer advocates and SDK authors who will bundle templates into the playground
- Solutions engineers running 10–30 minute client demos
- Early customers who need a super-compact onramp for POC work

Constraints and guiding principles:
- Keep each template < 10 files, single command to run after env setup
- Telemetry hooks prewired but disabled by default (opt-in)
- Local-first: work without network using a lightweight stub server (replay mode)
- Fail fast: explicit checklist showing where to look when things go wrong

Kit pieces (primitive building blocks):
1) init.sh / init.ps1 — bootstraps project, creates .env.example, copies sample prompt sets
2) run-local stub — tiny HTTP server that mimics Redwood responses for UI demos (node/python)
3) instrument.sh — wires telemetry: small JSON schema and metric names (latency_ms, tokens_sent, tokens_recv, error_code)
4) smoke-test script — automated check that key flows succeed (auth, generate, stream)
5) README-quick.md — 3-step set up + expected outputs + debugging hints

Quickflow template catalog (first wave):
- chat-web-demo (React + node stub): minimal chat page, streaming UI, fallback to local stub
- embed-search-probe (python + tiny index): ingest 10 docs, run vector search, show similarity scores
- cli-generate (go): CLI that sends prompt, streams output, prints token accounting
- webhook-batch-proxy (node): demonstrates batching fallback and retry semantics for sporadic traffic

Sample quickstart (chat-web-demo):
1) git clone && cd chat-web-demo
2) ./init.sh (creates .env.local, optional REDWOOD_API_KEY)
3) ./run-local-stub & npm start (starts stub and dev server)
4) open http://localhost:3000 — send a few messages, observe streaming and latency metrics
5) ./instrument.sh enable && run smoke-test (validates telemetry pipeline)

Telemetry & observability notes:
- Metric names must be stable across languages: redwood.quickflow.latency_ms, redwood.quickflow.tokens_sent, redwood.quickflow.errors.count
- Provide a small JSON map in repo root mapping SDK events -> Redwood Console breadcrumbs (so early users can correlate)
- Include an optional script to emit synthetic load so devs can demo batching behavior (burst to 50 QPS for 30s)

Developer ergonomics / DX heuristics:
- Single-copy environment variables: .env.local with example values; prefer short-lived API keys for demos
- Provide mental model: diagram in README-quick.md showing auth -> client -> runtime -> fallback
- Error copy: user-facing strings for common failures (401, 429, 5xx) and suggested remediations

Failure modes & playbook (quick):
- 401 on first call: check .env, ensure API key copied; run `./smoke-test --auth` to see header dump
- Streaming stalls: open devtools Network tab, confirm chunked responses; fallback to non-streaming route with `?stream=false` param
- Telemetry not appearing: run `./instrument.sh dump` to surface local JSON and check timestamps

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Do we bundle an ephemeral demo API key generator in CI for public playgrounds? pros/cons listed in TODOs
- Should telemetry be opt-in by default or opt-out? current lean: opt-in to respect privacy for external demos
- How many language templates in wave 1? target: node/python/go. Consider swift/android as stretch goal.

Next steps (MVP checklist):
- [ ] finalize metric name list and publish mapping to Console team (owner: Jonah)
- [ ] author README-quick for each template (owner: Mariana)
- [ ] add smoke-test harness and CI job to validate builds (owner: Ethan)
- [ ] land GH PRs linking kitgen examples to playground repo (PR: linked)

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a "guided tour" mode: thin overlay that points at UI elements and calls out what metric to watch in the Console
- Instructive failure: include a sample corrupt cache scenario to demonstrate cache invalidation + troubleshooting
- Create a single-file gist that shows the minimal SDK init pattern for all three languages (for blog snippet)

Slack threads / references:
- #devexp-kitgen current brainstorm thread (see linked_artifacts)
- GitHub PR 42 contains initial node/web demo skeleton

If you want to riff on one template, start with chat-web-demo — fastest feedback loop, easiest to demo streaming and error paths.

-- Aisha
